title: Complex behavior correlates with many cells being active at once

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complex behavior correlates with many cells being active at once

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In generalized mobile automata, complex behavior almost never occurs unless many cells are active simultaneously, and this correlation between overall activity and complexity helps explain why complexity is much more common in cellular automata than in mobile automata.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 3: The World of Simple Programs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: complex behavior almost never occurs except when large numbers of cells are active at the same time.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 3, “The World of Simple Programs”; section “Mobile Automata” (from p. 71), p. 76. Scope: mobile automata, generalized mobile automata and cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch03-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing computation can quantify the correlation in defined families. The causal explanation for cross-family prevalence and the vague frequency language prevent complete resolution across all generalized mobile automata.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sample or enumerate generalized mobile automata, measure the concurrent active-cell count and trajectory complexity, and estimate their association while controlling for rule description length and growth. Test whether complex cases below a preregistered activity threshold are genuinely rare.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Activity may be a consequence rather than a cause of complexity.

Almost never and large numbers lack thresholds.

The generalized rule space is large and sampling-sensitive.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.65
analysis feasibility: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Activity and a complexity score can both be computed on a sample of generalized mobile automata, so a correlation is measurable. The result is sensitive to how the two scores are defined, and a definition that treats proliferating activity as complexity restates the claim. Existing simulations can estimate a carefully separated correlation and cannot yet make it independent of those choices.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sample generalized mobile automata, score the number of simultaneously active cells, and score an independent complexity measure. The claim is confirmed if complex outcomes are rare in the low-activity bin and common in the high-activity bin. It is weakened if the complexity measure is defined in terms of activity itself.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The generalized rule space is sampled, not exhausted.

Almost never and large numbers of cells need cutoffs that can create or erase the correlation.

If complexity is read off the same activity pattern, the correlation is partly circular.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.48
